findings.title: VIEW permission on all groups grants global group manage permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin granted only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource passes canManage(). This is used by requireManage(), e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() for creating top-level groups, so a view-only FGAP admin can perform manage operations that should require the 'manage' scope. canManage() should check only MANAGE, unlike canView() which may accept VIEW or MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), groupResource.getId() is the authorization-store resource UUID, while group resources are named by the Keycloak group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() and hasPermission() looks up resources by name via findByName). Passing getId() to hasPermission() therefore never finds the per-group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, ignoring per-group view-members/manage-members grants. Adding groupResource.getId() to the result is also wrong: callers such as UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource put the returned values in UserModel.GROUPS to filter users by their actual group IDs, so even a successful check would filter by non-existent group IDs and return no members. Both places should use groupResource.getName().

findings.title: Missing all-groups resource causes NullPointerException instead of denying permission
findings.body: hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource() when a specific group resource is not found, but does not check whether that fallback resource is null before calling policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later resource.getScopes(). Realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the Groups resource type was introduced have no 'Groups' all-groups resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.init() only creates it when the client is first created), so any group permission check for such a realm, or any realm where that resource is absent, can throw an NPE/500 instead of returning false.
